text_fidelity_a:
MARK LAUREN Bodyweight Workout DVD Mobility Rx DVD Set I have owned this 2-DVD set for several weeks now, and I am still on the fence about it. I researched it thoroughly before I purchased it, and the overall reviews seemed very positive. I am a daily exerciser and also a yoga instructor, but as I get older (I'm 49 now), I definitely have increasing aches and pains, and I know there are times when my lack of flexibility limits my yoga practice. I was hoping that Mark Lauren's Mobility Rx set would benefit me in these areas.

I will first provide a brief overview of the workouts, then detail what I liked/didn't like. Both DVDs have a Main Menu which includes selection for Introduction (Lauren's 2-minute explanation of these workouts, which you can find on YouTube), Warm Up (the same for both workouts, and Workout (1 or 2). There is also an option for Music on/off and Closed Captioning on/off.

The Warm-up is what Lauren calls a "movement prep," and it clocks in at 9:39 minutes. In has nice, full-body joint mobility work such as windshield wiper knees, hydrant hip rotations, trunk rotations, one leg bridges, lunges with torso twist, squat, and lunges with lateral reach. Workout #1 is 34 minutes total, including a 4 1/2 minute description of each of the four exercises. (Note that it is NOT easy to skip this. You can select the workout from the Main Menu without doing the Warm-up, but it is also NOT easy to return to the Main Menu AFTER doing the Warm-up for some reason.) There are three rounds in this workout, and they clock in at 8:53, 9:22, and 11:12. The exercises are side-lying snow angel, isometric lunge, zombie squat, and scorpion complex, and they get progressively more challenging with each round. Workout #2 has the same structure but with different exercises. This workout is shorter, with 3 1/2 minute introduction and three rounds of 7:24, 7:37, and 8:14 to clock at 27 minutes total. The exercises are seated roll, straddle reach, spider crawl, and gate swing complex. All of the exercises are well-described in other reviews for those wanting more details.

What I like about Mobility Rx is much shorter than what I don't like, so I will start with that.

WHAT I LIKED ABOUT THESE WORKOUTS:
*The exercises themselves. For the most part, these felt like functional fitness movements that definitely have the potential to benefit my body.
*The Warm-up. Although almost 10 minutes is long for a warm-up, this would make a nice little stand-alone stretch routine; it could also work as a cool-down after other activity.

Okay, that's about all I can think of, so on to what I didn't like.

WHAT I DIDN'T LIKE ABOUT THESE WORKOUTS:
*The fact that they are on 2 separate DVDs. This may seem minor, but there's only a little over an hour of content, so making this set 2 separate DVDs not only feels wasteful to me but also feels like a marketing gimmick, as if they are trying to deceive customers.
*The very poor production values. Honestly, I often don't even notice these types of things on workout DVDs (and I have literally tried 100s), but there were MULTIPLE issues here, including the following: 1) the music - it was just bad, loud and on a repetitive loop (although at least there was a music off option), 2) the sound - it was out of sync with the screen, which is VERY annoying if you are actually looking at Lauren while doing the workout, 3) the menus - as mentioned above, options such as skipping forward and returning to the Main Menu did not work correctly, and 4) the set - also just awful, with a frame around the screen that appears as if you are looking into a 1980s computer and empty fake wood boxes stacked in the corner for no reason
*Lauren's instruction. Other than telling viewers to stand or sit with "tall PRETTY posture"--an awful expression that he uses over and over--he provides little instruction on form and absolutely no modifications. The initial preview of the exercises for each workout offers an anatomical view of the muscles being worked, but Lauren never refers back to this during the workouts themselves, never connecting the movements with the actual benefits for the body.
*The disparity between the two workouts. As you can see by my description above, the first workout is significant longer than the second, but it is also MUCH harder. The second exercise, the isometric lunge, is actually a lunge with the shin placed vertical against a wall/other structure. I would consider this an advanced movement--I have done it in yoga classes only after significantly more prep work than Lauren provides here. Similarly, the fourth exercise, scorpion complex, also incorporate yoga-type movements (plank and downward facing dog), and it requires a good deal of stamina and endurance.

In summary, I believe that these routines are appropriate ONLY FOR EXPERIENCED EXERCISERS. Although I definitely fall into that category myself, and I do see some utility to the movements Lauren offers here, the downsides of this set are a significant detraction for me, and I have not yet decided whether or not I will keep it.
text_fidelity_b: MARK LAUREN Bodyweight Workout DVD Mobility Rx DVD Set

The concept is very simple: expose it to bright light for a little while and it will glow in the dark for a longer while. The claim is that it will glow for up to 10 hours; I have not verified that it will last that long, but it does go for a long time, long enough in most situations that it will continue to glow long after sunset. This is really all I can ask.

The vial appears to be filled with some sort of phosphorous-coated granules. As a first test I exposed them to the bright light of an LED flashlight for about 30 seconds, and the vial glowed for several minutes afterward. It wasn’t all that bright, but I didn’t give it long to “charge” either. It was enough as a proof of concept though. It lasts longer under extended exposure to bright light such as direct sunlight.

The extra clips that come with the vial are useful for attaching it to other things without using the ring. One of the attachments is actually the same thing as a pen clip, which is useful for clipping to a tent flap, umbrella or other fabric surface.

Especially when considering the cost, this is really an easy product to recommend if you need a luminous marker. It really does work for a long while, it’s very easy to see and it is versatile.
text_fidelity_b: GEAR AID Ni Glo, 2” Glowing Keychain for Camping, Scuba and Night Fishing

text_fidelity_a:
Gaiam Pilates Total Toning Kit NOTE: I received a free copy of this workout kit to review for the web site Metapsychology Online Reviews.

Ana Cabán has been a mainstay of Pilates media for almost a decade now, but she is constantly adding new and varied challenges to her workouts. Here she includes 2-lb. hand weights fashioned into a unique "S" shape to increase the intensity of the program. The DVD offers three different 15-minute workouts, each of which incorporates the weights and yet are still based on the traditional exercises first introduced by Pilates founder, Joseph Pilates. Cabán works out alone in an outdoor setting; her purple mat is featured on a raised platform against a mountainous background. The music is generally pleasant and unobtrusive.

The Main Menu of the DVD offers options to select the Introduction, Mat Series, Equipment Series, or Standing Series. If you choose to start with the Mat Series as Cabán recommends, you can easily continue to complete the entire 54 minute workout, as there is only a brief pause between each section. In Mat Series (15 mins.), Cabán first uses the weights to move the arms from over the head to down towards her sides. Still holding the weights, Cabán does the Pilates Hundred move, keeping the weights still at her sides rather than pumping the arms as is customary. She continues with a classical Pilates matwork sequencing of movements, sometimes holding just one weight--for example, she performs Rolling Like a Ball holding one weight with both hands in front of the calves. All five exercises of the Series of Five are performed, using both weights for the first three exercises and just one weight for the last two. Cabán concludes the Mat Series in a seated position for the Spine Stretch forward (holding one weight behind the head) and the Spinal Twist (holding one weight straight out in front of the body).

The Equipment Series (19.5 mins.) is also performed entirely on the mat. Cabán begins with one weight in each hand for a move called Coordination and then continues on to the Rowing series, a sequence of several different classic Pilates exercises. Other exercises performed seated include Shaving the Head and Hugging a Tree. Still holding both weights, Cabán then moves to a prone (face-down) position for the Long Box series, which involves reaching the arms up and back as well as up and out to the sides. Next are several movements completed while on the back or seated, including a Back Stroke (again coordinating the movements of the arms and legs), a Teaser variation (holding the Teaser position while pumping the arms with the weights; repeat several times), and Short Box variations. After a brief side stretch, Cabán comes to a kneeling position, still using both weights for Chest Expansion, Thigh Stretch, Arm Circles, Bicep Curls, and Rolling In and Out. Cabán concludes this segment with the Mermaid, incorporating one weight at a time to increase the stretch.

The final segment is the Standing Series (19.5 mins.). Here Cabán beings in a standing position for Running in Place and Rolling through the Feet, adding in arm movements (holding both weights) to each of these exercises. These moves serve to pre-fatigue the upper body for a traditional series of Pilates arms work, including Bicep Curls, Tricep Extensions, Zip Ups, The Bug, Little Circles, and Boxing. For many of these exercises, Cabán begins with the heels grounded but then rises onto the toes as she repeats the exercise. She continues to hold both weights for all of the remaining moves, which include Lunges, Side Bend, "Hide Your Hands," Pick a Flower, Wall series, Arm Lifts, Arm Circles, and finally, Roll-Downs.

Overall, I was very impressed with this workout kit. The design of the S-weights seemed very ergonomic in nature, as they were extremely comfortable to use, offered even distribution of the weight, and were very easily incorporated into the flow of the workouts. Given this, I actually felt the exercises more intensely than I ever have before. I consider myself to be an a perennial intermediate level in Pilates; although I have always enjoyed Pilates matwork, I have never gotten much out of the other Pilates exercises--e.g., the Rowing series, the Pilates Arms work, etc.--in the past. But Cabán's distinctive method of putting these movements together along with the S-weights truly made a difference.

Cabán does not mirror-cue, but she has an excellent, easygoing instruction style; she does assume some pre-existing familiarity with basic Pilates moves here. In summary, I would highly recommend this workout set, particularly for intermediate level and above Pilates practitioners.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Pilates Total Toning Kit

The threads felt very dicey.

Also I think than in my own experience using a riser was a bad idea. I was having a hard time getting comfortable on my road bike (contemporary Trek) but I noticed that on my 90's Trek the bars were slammed by comparison and that bike is very comfortable. text_fidelity_a:
Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips 2.0 - Extreme Arm Blaster - Best Dumbbell and Barbell Thick Bar Adapter (Charcoal) --Preamble--

Like many people, I decided to try out some thick bar grips to optimize my current regimen. I too was attracted by the idea of improving my grip and strengthening the whole complex of muscles/tendons/ligaments in my forearms. So I purchased four kinds of wide bar grips - Fat Gripz One (1.75"), Fat Gripz Pro (2.25"), Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips (2"), and Yes4All Thick Bar Grips (2.2").

Before the review, some context:

First, you should ease into these things, and so if you aren't accustomed to thick bar grips, I would recommend you start with the Fat Gripz One. I did not do this; I tried to integrate all four into my routine, and as a result I gave myself acute tendonitis in both arms, in the form of Golfer's Elbow. Now I need to take at least 4 weeks off while I heal up, and no one likes that. I don't think this would have been a problem if I just started with the narrower grips and moved up from there.

Second, if use a ruler, my hand is 6 5/8" (168mm) from the bend of the wrist to the tip of my middle finger. The Fat Grips One is fine, the Iron Bull Strength grips are about the limit of decent grip, and the Fat Grips Pro are too large to get my hand around, limiting me to fairly light dumbbells. For pull-ups, only the Fat Grips one are comfortable, the Iron Bull's are marginal. I have chronic issues with my TFCC (something I was hoping to help alleviate through these grips) and the thicker ones tend to aggravate that complex.

Lastly, I am fairly fit. I am about 183lbs (83.2kg) and was doing sets of 23 pull-ups before this. I could maintain those numbers with the narrower wide grips, but with greater effort. I have my pull-up bar (an Iron Gym) wrapped in racket grip tape, so it is about 1.1" in diameter. Most of my dumbbells have bars that are between 1.1 and 1.25" in diameter.

--Product Review--

The Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips 2.0 are a respectable alternative to the Fat Gripz. They have a different profile, being more curved in the center, which I don't necessarily prefer, but it isn't really a negative, just different. They are firmer than Fat Gripz, but not much less grippy. I prefer how they look, being all black, no colored logos to distract the eye. As for the scent, they smell like coconut oil to me, which is pleasant.

---Comfort

The Iron Bull Alpha Grips are fairly comfortable, not as much as the Fat Gripz Pro but close. Like other thick bar grips they have a raised pattern pressed into the rubber which give more of an inconsistent surface than an uncomfortable one. The suitability of the raised bump in the middle is going to be highly subjective; I personally like it on dumbbells, but not on my pull-up bar. These have a seam, just like all thick bar grips, though it is smaller than some cheaper models. These don't fit on IronMaster dumbbells due to them having a 1.25" bar, but they fit CAP models and my pull-up bar, an Iron Gym, pretty well. I find the 2" diameter is much nicer to work with than the 2.25" of the Fat Gripz Pro.

---Benefit

Decent benefit, it has an immediately noticeable visual effect, within a week anyway. I had to drop 20% of my reps to compensate, but before the injury I could feel the improvements already, such that it felt odd not to use them. Whereas before the IronMaster bar felt thick, now it feels fairly thin. Definitely helps improve general muscle tone and forearm strength and feels, at least, like the exercises are more engaging. Effect is as described, and I imagine one would see real benefits in muscle mass within a month.

---Conclusion

I'd recommend these as a solid alternative to the Fat Gripz, not necessarily better or worse, but merely different. Presently, I like the Fat Gripz One for pull-ups, the Fat Gripz Pro for light weights (<30lb), and the Iron Bull Alpha Grips 2.0 for medium weights (30lb-55lb).
text_fidelity_b: Iron Bull Strength Alpha Grips 2.0 - Extreme Arm Blaster - Best Dumbbell and Barbell Thick Bar Adapter (Charcoal)

text_fidelity_a:
NordicTrack T Series Treadmills My primary concerned based on other reviews was that the motor would be noisy. That depends entirely on the speed. If you want it as a walking treadmill, you will definitely hear your footfalls much louder. You could whisper above the motor, no problem. If you are a casual runner and want to take it to say 6 miles an hour (that's pretty much a 30 minute 5K) it's quiet. You can sort of hear it, but not a lot. If you are a pro athlete and want to take it to 10 miles an hour, first off, respect, and second off, you will hear noise about the equivalent to a car engine on the highway.

The iFit attachment, which I recommend, doesn't come with it. You need to buy it, and the subscription, separately. It enables you to download a series of training programs via WiFi including what may be the world's easiest C25K program. They call it Beginner 5K. It's 4 times a week for 12 weeks. It starts with you casually strolling along on the treadmill for half a mile in 15 minute (think the average walking pace of a senior citizen) but it ends with you running uphill at about 5 miles an hour (at that rate you could finish a 5K in roughly 40 minutes) and there are no sudden transitions. It just creeps up the incline a little, then the speed, and soon the fast pace of the old level is the resting pace of the new, but it feels like a resting pace. You build fitness gradually. The treadmill has some pre-programmed routes and workouts built in, and the site has a great many more. My only complaint is there is no way to preview the list before subscribing, to know if it's worth it. Set up for that was a bit of a pain, more so than I'd expected.

I found the left speaker a little weaker than the right, but that could be an audio trick used by Zombies, Run! Otherwise, the sound system is nice. It plugs in via a standard audio cable, not Blutooth in an era where standard audio cables are going out of fashion. There are adapters if that becomes an issue. There are holders for water and phone, etc, and a nice ledge for an ipad.

I like the cushioning, and it is adjustable. I like how easy it is to fold up. Mind, assemble this where you mean to keep it. You're not going to fold it and stuff it in a closet. It's way too heavy for that. Installation takes two people, especially at the end when you have to hold the bottom unit up to install the hydraulic lift. I needed to check a video for that part.

The off switch is to take the little key off the panel. You can use the reset button on the bottom, if you've set it up to be conveniently accessible, but it takes a lot longer to come back from that. It actually takes longer to come back from that, than from shutting of the surge protector it's plugged into, which makes me think it is doing some sort of reset processing. It definitely needs a surge protected, and I recommend the NordicTrack brand for this, just to be safe.

Overall, I'd say this is a high quality treadmill at a reasonable price.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills

Others have covered the myriad of uses, so I will confine my review to some features that I like and other aspects that I tested.

One of the nicest features is the fact that you can clip this on to a belt loop, shirt of even a helmet (using the short strips of velcro and some glue). As I was testing these I did notice that while the clip is convenient, it may be TOO convenient. It's so easy to attach to a piece of apparel that you may wind up clipping it to a pocket that obscures it if you are wearing a loose over shirt. That is not a flaw in the design as much as my giving a head's up that how you use it is important.

The light is not super bright (nor should it be since you do not want to distract drivers), so if you absolutely want to be seen the flash mode is perfect on dark, unlit streets and roads. Also, for biking or walking I recommend using both lights - one in the back and one in the front of your person - so that you can be seen from both directions.

While the product specs do not claim this is waterproof I did submerge one of the lights in a sink of water for two minutes and it remained operational. It may not be actually waterproof, but will not fail in inclement weather.

Overall, this is a great way to remain safe on foot or bike, and the lights are nicely built.

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Freeze Dried Whole Blueberries 12 oz No. 10 Can Get what you can, while you can. Spend now, or spend even more later (and that is if food is available). Doesn't need to be emergency packed food. Buy extra of what you like to eat every single time you are at the store, shop sales, go frequently (don't wipe out shelves). If you are at a spot where you want to add greater variety to put into long term storage, then Augason tends to have quality products and better prices than other emergency brands. Look for their sales, shop often, build up your supplies.

I like adding blueberries into the mix as it reconstitutes well, has good flavor and texture, and is still loaded with nutrients. Easy enough to stock up on rice and beans, harder to stock up on fruits and vegetables. Grow what you can, freeze or can what you can.. and buy what you can. Freeze dried is a very nice way to get good food that is still nutritious.

Most #10 (that reads, "number ten" not ten pound) cans will maintain freshness and quality for 10-25 years after production date. If opened, it will be shorter; depends on what you get. Blueberries in my experience are perfectly fine for a long time. Environmental factors will impact this. The cans are pest proof, can take a beating (even if dented should be fine as foods are freeze dried and have no moisture to sustain bacterial growth), can float if not opened, and are a standard size for stacking and uniformity (hence why weights will vary, and some stuff only fills a little of can).
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Freeze Dried Whole Blueberries 12 oz No. 10 Can

text_fidelity_a:
WINNINGO Portable Bike Floor Pump Every cyclist needs to carry a portable pump and an extra tube with them at all times. If you happen to get a flat ten miles away from your home, you are out of luck. You can't try to ride on a flat tire because it's dangerous and you'll ruin both the tire and the rim. It's a much better practice to have a high quality pump.

This Winningo portable pump is a perfect choice. The gauge takes out the guesswork and you can use this pump to get back to your regular tire pressure and continue with your ride. The valve can easily be converted between Presta and Schrader. The valve is attached to a rubber tube which makes inflation a lot more convenient. Many portable pumps attach directly to the valve stem, and if you're not careful you can accidentally snap off the stem when you inflate. The rubber tube makes that unfortunate outcome virtually impossible.

This portable pump is designed like a mini floor pump. It stands upright and a foot pedal flips out for stability. This allows you to pump up your tire with the assistance of body weight. You can easily inflate a tire to its recommended pressure with this pump, but the pump is compact enough to fit on a clip beside a water bottle cage on the downtube. This is a great product that will ensure you are well equipped to get back out on the road if you ever have a flat during a ride.
text_fidelity_b: WINNINGO Portable Bike Floor Pump

Heated Gloves for Women Touchscreen Rechargeable Battery Electric Hand Warmers Winter Gloves Ski Gloves for Outdoor Sports Cycling Riding Skiing Skating I’ve never owned heated gloves before, but these are amazing! The design allows you to easily tighten several areas of the glove for a better fit, and you can still use your smart phone with the fingertips, which is great. The batteries have light indicators to show you roughly how charged they are, and they are easy to put in to the glove and remove, as well as to charge. Turning the gloves on and off it’s also as simple as the press of a button on top, which is easy to operate even while wearing the gloves.

As for the heat distribution, it’s not as even as I would like: it is most concentrated at the thumb and doesn’t distribute as much to the other areas. Even so, it’s incredibly soothing and pleasant, and on the most frigid days, boy does it make a difference! There are three levels of intensity for the heat, so you can decide what feels best. For me, I either like 45% or 70%. The hottest setting (100%), because it’s so concentrated in the thumb, feels a little uncomfortable for me personally. These were so straightforward on how to use them, I didn’t need the instruction manual, but I read it anyway just to see if I was missing anything. I learned there is a spare cable in case the one inside the glove wears out for whatever reason, which is nice.

Overall, these are excellent for cold weather and people whose hands get particularly cold. Even off-season, if you have arthritis or any hand pain, these are terrific for that as well. Terrific invention!
text_fidelity_b: Heated Gloves for Women Touchscreen Rechargeable Battery Electric Hand Warmers Winter Gloves Ski Gloves for Outdoor Sports Cycling Riding Skiing Skating

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Upslope Snowsports Backpack, 35 L This pack was designed for back-country skiing. For a detailed look at the design and features of the book I highly recommend checking out Thule's video in the listing. It's very well shot, quickly gets to the point, and gives a complete overview of the features. That being said, here's my review on this versatile piece of travel gear.

I ride longboard skateboards, and the snowboard attachment is perfect for holding a decent sized deck. Even if you don't have a use for the ski or snowboard attachments they tuck neatly away and the bag still has perfect functionality for travel or hiking. It's light, durable and has strong seams and zippers. There are multiple compartments for ease of access for different types of items, though the largest compartment opens from behind the straps and the bag must be removed before you can access it.

One of the most clever features is a well engineered elastic interior. The bag is very compressed but expands with the load that you place in the main compartment. It can expand to 35 liters, which is quite impressive, but it also will hold much less than that securely without sagging or getting off balance. That is what makes this bag for me - it's versatile whether you're traveling for either a weekend or a full week.

Provided that you load the bag securely according to Thule's recommendations, this bag is very comfortable when strapped on your back. A chest and waist strap are included to share the load, and they work very well to disperse the weight evenly. The shoulder straps fit high and feel very secure when adjusted properly, and they don't pull at your back like many other packs can.

All of the pockets, seams, zippers and hardware are top quality and appear to be made to last. I'll be heading on a trip to Europe soon and will be taking this as my carry-on (it won't fit fully loaded under a seat but will fit in an overhead fine). I have a feeling this bag is going to be first in my list of travel gear for a long time. I definitely recommend picking one up.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Upslope Snowsports Backpack, 35 L

text_fidelity_a:
WLOOD Golf Cart Speaker Mount, Universal Portable Adjustable Strap Fits Most Bluetooth Wireless Speakers Attachment Accessory Holder Bar Rail Who wouldn’t love some great tunes on their golf cart..?!! As a family who owns a golf cart yet, has never golfed a day in our life - we’ve spent the last decade doing nothing but, fun rides and adventures all around our planned community with our kiddos on this toy. Music would only enhance this- and give us golf cart karaoke?!!

Problem is.. this is a one size fits most. But, it didn’t come close to being “most” for us! How.. when we have the same speaker used in the sellers sample photo description- see photo I included..??!! Right from start when trying to attach we had issues.. this has 6 velcro straps coming out of the sides- (picture a big bug with legs!) Zero instructions included and you'd think this would be straightforward.. Trust me, we tried straps forward wrapping around pole and then, backwards just the same- we even went back to description online.. studied the photo and still had no success.

Problems we incurred:

•Straps are not long enough to wrap around the pole and speaker- and have enough length to close on themself. (this is placing the speaker in same spot as advertised!)

•2 of the 3 sets of straps were sewn in backwards- so, if wrapping around the direction they’re attached- The Velcro teeth on x2 straps are on the wrong side. (Equivalent to getting two negative signs together..) hoping this is an error!

•From photo description it appears we are missing a middle extra strap? Photo shows x1 in brown strap thru middle but, we don’t have anything of the sort...??

•This has no bottom support or “shelf” for added protection.. this could lead speaker slide at the bottom if it were to become a loose. Golf carts bounce around a bit and vibration may cause this to slip. So, bottom support would be helpful if not, necessary to protect the speaker from falling down and give the user peace of mind.

•This is missing a simple but straightforward set of instructions.

overall, this may work with a much smaller size speaker- one with hardly any girth.. Even then, it may be hit/miss to get the securely fastened. I’m afraid a smaller speaker may not produce enough sound to be heard over a motorized golf cart and will it stay safe? In leui of listing this “one size fits all/most..” this would be beneficial to list the actual length and dimension of straps so, one can verify speaker sizes that would work! Listed at a price point of $10- this could be a great find.. if, it could be successful. Tbh, It may be safer to invest more solid option to ensure it will fit/function as expected. I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: WLOOD Golf Cart Speaker Mount, Universal Portable Adjustable Strap Fits Most Bluetooth Wireless Speakers Attachment Accessory Holder Bar Rail

However, this laser is powerful enough to do some serious eye damage! It's powerful enough to pop a dark colored balloon if held in place for a moment. In fact, it's powerful enough that if I point it at the back of my hand and hold it in place for a few seconds, it begins to sting! That's more than bright enough to permanently damage your pet's eyes, especially if you're pointing it towards them in order to get them to chase after it. Lasers like these are not currently well regulated on this site, so you should not assume that they are safe. I'd advise wearing proper laser safety goggles when using this laser, never point it towards a person, and please don't use it to play with your pets!

And now that I've got that diatribe out of the way, the product itself seems fairly well made, and at a decent price. It has a nice protector ring that covers the "on" button to help prevent accidental discharge. This helps with safety, as well as keeping your battery from draining due to accidental use. The beam is pretty well focused, and I don't see much diffusion even 50-100 feet out. On a cloudy day, the laser point (not the beam, but the spot where it is pointed) is clearly visible at 100-200 feet of distance. At night, the beam itself is clearly visible in the atmosphere.

Daelizi 2-Pack/A+ Protection Mouth Guard, Sports Mouthguard for Boxing，Football, Lacrosse, Hockey, Basketball, Flavored Mouth Guard, Adult (Black) While I don't box or play football such that it requires me wearing a mouthpeice, I do grind my teeth at night, which is what I used this for.

There are times, especially when there is a lot going on, I tend to grind my teeth at night. So instead of buying those expensive mouth-pieces I just use the ones for sports. Follow the instructions to help mold the peice to your mouth. If you don't like the lanyard, just give it a good yank to pull it out of the mouthpiece, but do that AFTER you have molded the peice to the mouth so you have something to hold onto while softening it in hot water.

Double-Bonus that it comes in a nice hany case for travel or storage use. The lanyard to attach the piece to a helpmet is nice so you don't lose the peice in case an impact causes it to fall out.

The product arrived well packaged. Each mouthpiece, if you order more than one, will be individually wrapped.

Even though it says its flavored, I really didn't notice any flavor at all. Which is kinda misleading but doesn't detract from its intended purpose. Would recommend the the company take that part out, cause its misleading and actually may shy folks away from the product.

As for value, you get two in a package for a decent price, whereas its not uncommon to pay for a comparable product at 2/3 the price.

Disclosure: I did receive this product for free to review through the Amazon Vine program.
text_fidelity_b: Daelizi 2-Pack/A+ Protection Mouth Guard, Sports Mouthguard for Boxing，Football, Lacrosse, Hockey, Basketball, Flavored Mouth Guard, Adult (Black)

text_fidelity_a: RockyMounts Hendrix Compact Folding Bicycle Lock This is an interesting bicycle lock. It weighs about 1.5 pounds and folds up to the size of a water bottle. It unfolds to about the same size as a standard U-lock and can lock your bike in most places where you could use a U-lock. There is enough space to lock your frame and rear wheel to a bike rack. U-locks are 2 pounds and up, so this lock saves weight and is smaller and easier to carry. It is certainly more secure than any cable lock which are always easy to cut with hand tools. The steel plates are not real thick (about 3mm), but because of their width, I have to imagine they are safer than a lightweight slightly thicker chain lock when attacked by bolt cutters. I do worry about how safe the joints are. The manufacturer claims a safety rating of 7/10, but this is their own rating, there is no industry standard rating system in the USA.

Coleman Camping Instant Signal Mountain Tent This arrived today and I was very anxious to try to set it up. We camped a lot when I was a child and setting up the tent always involved a lot of cussing on someone's part. This wasn't too different an experience in some ways.

Pros:

Fairly easy to set up the first time out of the box. I did it by myself.
Lightweight enough for a woman to carry
Large floor space and tall enough for a 6' 2" man to stand up in.
Lots of vents and windows
Nice rainfly

Cons:
Impossible directions. You don't need them too much to get set up, but you need some guidance to get the tent down and back in the bag. It took 3 tries to finally get it in there
The center beam on the top that keeps the tent stretched out, did not lock in place for us. I don't know if this is a defect or just poor design
Because of the lightweight nature of this, the floor and walls are very thin material. The floor reminds me of one of those really cheap plastic tarps that you can get.
The metal stakes that are used to hold in the feet of the poles bend very easily if you hit a rock or an obstacle.
Not very secure when set up. I think this would need some serious tent stakes to hold it down in any kind of wind. It was windy here today and I'm not sure this would have stayed together too long.
The zippers are not going to take much use, in fact the whole thing might be good for one season of regular camping and use/abuse.

All in all, I was hoping for better. At least something that kids visiting us could use. Maybe with a little tweaking we can get it stable.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Instant Signal Mountain Tent

AMTOP Portable Solar Panel Collapsible Clover Camping Tent Lantern Lighting Lights Flashlight for Hiking/Camping/Jogging/Emergencies/Hurricanes/Outages (Green) I received this as a free review sample. Since the product specs are very detailed I am not going to repeat them, but will say that they are pretty accurate based on my testing them for over six hours.

One thing that is missing from the product specs is this lantern is easily water resistant in rain and wet environments. The cover for the USB port is effective. That is not to say that it would work submerged in water for more than a few inches, but in a storm it definitely works well. One big feature that I like is it uses a micro USB port to charge. Contrast that with a lot of lights (solar and conventional) that employs a USB cable with a barrel type connector. Those kinds will work from a standard charger, but you are out of luck if you lose that cable while camping or damage it in an emergency unless you are one of the rare folks who has a spare. With this one you can use any micro USB cable.

To set expectations, this is meant to be solar charged in emergencies. That takes forever. Well, every hour yields .25 to .5 hours of use time, depending on your brightness setting. Also, this is not a super bright light on the highest setting. It is more than sufficient for emergency illumination and the flash function can be seen from afar, but it is not strong enough for detailed inspections, reading and similar activities.

For me the compact, light form factor, water resistance, and the fact that it uses a standard micro USB port are its best features. If it has any Achilles heel, it's the hanging hook that seems a little on the fragile side and will accommodate a rod (or twig) about 3/16ths an inch in diameter. Based on price versus features, though, I still felt that it rated five stars given similar products.
text_fidelity_b: AMTOP Portable Solar Panel Collapsible Clover Camping Tent Lantern Lighting Lights Flashlight for Hiking/Camping/Jogging/Emergencies/Hurricanes/Outages (Green)

text_fidelity_a:
Harbinger Flexfit Ultra WristWrap Lifting Gloves I have owned a pair of Lee Haney lifting gloves with wrist wrap for 19 years and which I used three times per week for about 12 of those years. I still have those gloves and although they are a bit stiff, you'd never know they were used so much as they hardly look worn. Since the Lee Haney gloves are not padded, I decided to try these gloves both because I expected an increase in comfort and as an enticement to get me back into lifting again.

The gloves I received are a size "Large" and they are heavier than any other lifting gloves I've tried before; the pair weighs in at 6.2 ounces according to my dietary food scale. However, you don't notice the weight when wearing them. Below are the pros and cons I noticed during use:

PROS:

1. The gloves are well padded. In fact, the padding is an excellent feature for when I perform lifts where the weight is in the palm of my hand, such as when doing a bench press or incline press or when the weight is evenly distributed throughout the hand such as when doing squats using a [[ASIN:B0000AVAL2 Advanced Fitness Manta Ray]].

2. I usually take a size medium or large in a woman's glove and this size large fit me comfortably.

3. The extra "leather-like" flap that you secure to the fastened wrist wrap offers extra security so that the wrap won't come undone during a lift and the gloves will remain securely fastened.

CONS:

1. The padding on the pinkie finger was uncomfortable for me when doing dead lifts because the bar was evenly distributed through my hand and the padding on the pinkie finger seemed to get in the way. It almost caused a pressure point of discomfort during each entire lift (ascent and descent).

2. The wrist wrap was awkward to fasten because not only did I have to wrap the strap around my wrist, but then I had to flip over the "leather-like" flap and make sure it fastened to the Velcro on the back of the flap.

3. I was bothered by the white tag inside the right glove during lifting. Perhaps the manufacturer could either leave the tags out or put them on the non-Velcro portion of the wrist wrap.

4. I don't like that the two pieces of fabric used to fasten the glove to the cardboard insert it came with remain sewed to the glove. Basically, the gloves arrive with two tags on each glove that fastens to the cardboard packaging. Those tags remain as part of the glove and to me they are annoying as I see no reason to ever use those tags again.

I do think that if men are considering purchasing these gloves, they might want to consider ordering the next size up. My boyfriend always takes a size "Large" in men's gloves and he had to struggle to get these size Large gloves on his hands.

These gloves are thick and although they feel well-made they don't look well-made on close inspection. Therefore, I'm concerned that the stitching on the padding may come loose. When comparing these gloves to my Lee Haney gloves, I doubt they will last as long but only time will tell.

If padding is important, then these gloves offer that and certainly cushion the lifter during many lifts. However, for me I can only give these gloves an average rating because of the cons and my concern that the stitching around the padding will come loose.
text_fidelity_b: Harbinger Flexfit Ultra WristWrap Lifting Gloves

text_fidelity_a:
Bowflex 4.1 Bench Black./Red This isn't our first FID (flat, incline, decline) bench, but while it has less features than some, it's exactly what we needed now. While our previous benches were rated for more weight and took more attachments, we like this one as it's lighter and smaller than the other ones - not light and small, exactly, as it is still rated for 450 pounds including user and weight, but still smaller. The foot holddown is adjustable, and while there aren't as many positions for the back as there are on some benches, including the newer version of this bench, there are enough. Also the seat adjusts, which wasn't true of the previous model, the 4.1.

We got this bench rather than the 5.1 version because we found a 4.1 we could actually try in person, and it was great for both my 6' 7" husband and me (i'm 5' 3"). The 5.1 version has the u-shaped front support, but the straight one on this bench works fine.

The only thing we don't love about it is that the gap between the seat and back is pretty wide in some positions, but that's normal with FID benches with thicker seats. Throw a towel between the two sections or cut a piece of foam out to the exact shape and slide whichever into the gap as needed.

We like our Bowflex SelectTech 4.1 bench a lot. It's stable, sturdy and does the job as long as you don't need a bench that is rated over 450 pounds total (which these days we don't need). It doesn't fold up, but it's smaller than a lot of the higher rated benches, and the foot holddown does the job well. If you're looking for a super light, small bench or a bench rated 600 pounds or more, this isn't the bench for you. If you're like us, under 250 pounds and wanting to work out with 200 pounds or less, this bench has the flexibility to enhance your workouts and the padding is pretty comfortable, too.

text_fidelity_a:
Thule Apex XT Bike Hitch Rack I ordered the ‘Thule Apex XT Swing 4 Bike Hitch Rack’ for review. I liked that the design of the Thule Apex XT which allows you to swing the rack (while installed and loaded) out and away, so that you can open your back hatch while your bikes are installed on the rack. My other hitch style bike rack does not allow this, and I have to remove the bikes to access my back hatch. I have assembled, installed and used the Thule Apex XT bike rack for some time now and would like to share my thoughts.

I would firstly like to get out of the way some of the other complaints I have read about the assembly of this particular Thule bike rack. Basically it comes shipped in two main parts. The complaint is that the main bolt that connects these two parts was too tight and many people ended up breaking something and complained that the two parts and bolt did not assemble correctly. I would like to say that for me, (after reading the issues people were having) I was a bit concerned. BUT, I really had no issue at all. Yes it was a bit difficult to install the said bolt, but that is absolutely to be expected with the way the two pieces connect. Basically all I did was to line up the parts the best I could, stick the bolt in the top hole and slightly jiggle the rack assembly while putting downward pressure on the bolt until it fell into place. Yes it was a snug fit, but really there was no issue. After these two parts are assembled, there will be no need to take them apart again.

With that out of the way, I would like to say that I have never owned a Thule product but have always wanted to because of the brand reputation. So far in my opinion, this really is a quality product, however I do feel that it’s a bit overpriced compared to other brands out there that are also well built and of good quality and design. The features that this rack offers however, such as the “swing out” design, built in bike lock cable and easy hitch mount with lock included, makes this particular model very appealing and a feature packed value. I guess what I am trying to say is that there is absolute value to the Thule Apex XT bike rack if you could find it on sale.

Build quality in my opinion is great but I do notice that there is a lot of plastic and my concern would be, how well will it hold up over time? Fortunately the plastic parts used are not part of the main construction, rather more for cosmetics and if they do crack or break, it shouldn’t affect the functionality of the bike rack itself.

Others have mentioned, and I have noticed it myself that there is a bit of rattle in the unit but because of the way it’s designed, that is inevitable. It’s not going to fall apart or off your hitch for that matter as long as you have assembled it correctly of course but the rattle is noticeable.

Now for the ONLY real issue I have is that my daughters (oddly shaped) 26” frame does not fit on this rack unfortunately. I know that there is an adapter that is available from Thule, but I honestly don’t think that it would work with the way her frame is designed. All of our other bikes work great and securely with this rack, but if I am to take her bike, I will have to use my other rack.

Overall, I think this is a well made quality “hitch mount” bike rack with great features but beware that some bikes won’t fit, and you may be better off with another model that supports the bikes from the tires which will allow more compatibility.
text_fidelity_b: Thule Apex XT Bike Hitch Rack

KUGOO Electric Scooter, 800W Motor Off-Road Scooter, 10-INCH Pneumatic Tires Up to 25 MPH Motorized Adult Scooter, Electric Scooter for Adults, Pro Scooter, G2 PRO I have 7 scooters I've collected along the way to review and hands down this is the most fun one out there! If you're familiar with how an electric scooter works then this one is just like the others and will be easy to setup and get going. Took me about five minutes to unbox and get going! Even for newbies this scooter is plenty easy to setup!

One of the favorite things I love on this are the giant wheels- we ride on a concrete trail several miles across town and this absolutely grabs onto the concrete very well and is a better overall ride! My one complaint is the tires must be thin as on my fourth ride, one of them got a flat even though I didn't hit anything noticeable like glass or a screw. Nothing in the tire but it just started losing pressure on a ride and within a couple minutes the tire was completely flat and I was stuck pushing it home a mile. My suggestion is to get the tire size off the tire and immediately swap them out for solid tires! The air tires are a slightly smoother ride but you'll regret it when you're stuck pushing it home...
Edit: The air leaks out of the valve stem. I went to add some green slime and it did hold air but when I moved the valve stem, air comes out at the bottom of it... So the valve stem was faulty and the slime didn't help anything. I've been searching like crazy with no luck finding a solid tire to replace these with. Should have been on the scooter to begin with in my opinion.

Speed wise, I got this monster up to 29 mph and I'm a larger man (260 pounds) so that's a testament to this thing! It stands higher than your average scooter too which is weird at first but I fell in love with the added height nearly instantly!

It has a faster startup than other scooters that require more of a kick start. Which- be careful, that can be dangerous if you have the scooter on and are pushing it to park it before turning it off. I almost flipped mine backwards onto myself this way, it happens QUICK. So definitely turn the scooter (and any scooter) off before pushing around.

Battery life is fantastic- we ride several miles across town and back and I still have half a battery left after that!

Overall this is my favorite thing I've gotten on review and I've gotten big fancy electronics like big TVs, computers, etc... But this is my favorite toy I've grabbed, I HIGHLY recommend it! In the future I'll absolutely be buying another from this company!
text_fidelity_b: KUGOO Electric Scooter, 800W Motor Off-Road Scooter, 10-INCH Pneumatic Tires Up to 25 MPH Motorized Adult Scooter, Electric Scooter for Adults, Pro Scooter, G2 PRO

Kulie AllSport Bicycle Trunk Bag 38L Waterproof Pannier Bag for Front Rear Bike Rack Pannier Bags for Rear Seat Cargo Bag Rear Pack Trunk Pannier Handbag Saddle Bag for Bicycle Front Rack I have mixed feelings about this bag, with some positive and negative features

One issue is its attachment, which is via six velcro straps--two on the bottom and one on each corner/side. On the one hand, that means it's pretty universal, so you don't have to worry if it can go on your rack. On the other hand, it isn't 100% universal, and it's also nowhere near as solidly attached as most high-level bags. On my rack, for instance, the two bottom velcro straps don't work very well--the one toward the seat has little way to attach and due to having a seat bag, it's also tough to get my fingers in there. The four side ones aren't an issue, but with all the straps attach, I can't say I feel wholly confident with just how strongly it is attached to my bike. There's still some movement, and you'll most likely really want to be sure your bag is balanced, which isn't something I worry about with any of the my other biking bags. Honestly, I'd probably bungy the bag to feel wholly confident. Being velcro, I'd also be concerned about how well they'll maintain their attachment abilities over time and weather. In short, it's an inexpensive and more universal way to go, but it offers nowhere near the stability, immovability, or confidence as better attachment modes

The storage is nicely flexible, with a number of pockets and a removable separator in the main compartment, which is nicely padded. The fold-out exandable pockets are a nice touch, and I think will generally be quite convenient for lighter goods. My 16' MacBook isn't going to fit, and even if it did, I'd be worried about its weight over time, and about the lack of padding. I now it says it can handle "laptops", but I'm not super confident about that. But certainly my iPad will go in with room to spare and I wouldn't worry about the weight weakening the pocket. Folder, papers, light clothing, or groceries that aren't too heavy could all go in there. I like the number of compartments, the padding on several, and the ability to expand as needed.

The webbing on top is also nice to either attach things to or to hold a jacket or the like, which is does with a good sense of confidence it won't slip out.

If they could improve the attachment mode, this would be a good or very good bag. As is, I'd call it a value bag that is sufficient for non-expensive items, such as for small grocery runs, a bike to the park where you're carrying a disc and some food and drink, etc.
text_fidelity_b: Kulie AllSport Bicycle Trunk Bag 38L Waterproof Pannier Bag for Front Rear Bike Rack Pannier Bags for Rear Seat Cargo Bag Rear Pack Trunk Pannier Handbag Saddle Bag for Bicycle Front Rack

But sadly, the padding -- which I saw on the Medium and fervently hoped would be bigger on the XL -- was still child sized. Adults have more surface area to fall on. These pads were narrow and small, targeting very small areas that one can easily miss during a fall. Also, I barely felt cushioned when I tried gently bumping my tailbone. The hips I didn't feel the padding on at all because I missed no matter how many times I tried falling while aiming for the padding.

The pads' holes are a smart idea to reduce weight, and the idea of breathable cotton shorts with packets sewn on for gel padding is a great idea that gets rid of the hassle of placing akton gel on each spot e.g. the famous skatingsafe gel gear that must be held in place with stinky synthetic tights. But unlike the akton gel, these gel pads, while squishy when pushed with a finger, don't seem to provide the same shock absorption. For now, I will stick to my puffy foam shorts as they provide more noticeabpe protection. I hope this company improves their design and I'd be the first to come back.

And a good choice for the task is the Backyard Champs 2 x 4 Cornhole Carry Bag.

I got hold of this bag at the same time that I obtained a cornhole set, also from Backyard Champs. The idea of a carrying bag made sense, so I added it to my order. The bag is black in color and seals shut with Velcro flaps. It measures two feet in width, four feet in length, and eight inches in thickness. Thus, it has enough space to hold the cornhole set I own, which is from the same company. However, it may not be the correct size for other sets, so make sure you measure first.

The carrying handles on this bag are a little thinner than expected. They are also looped more widely than I feel they should be. A little less width, more like a briefcase handle, would seem better. The cornhole set I have isn’t too heavy so I think the handles will hold up, but there is still a little more looseness than I prefer. I hope I am proven wrong and that the manufacturer knew what they were doing when they designed the bag, but it just seems a little too loose for me. I suppose they made the loop larger so that you can place the handle over your shoulder but I prefer to carry it more like a suitcase.

Cornhole sets are often bulky and they need to be protected when transporting from one place to another. A carrying bag makes sense and the Backyard Champs 2 x 4 Cornhole Carry Bag is a good choice for the task. A little more snug fit and a separate compartment for the bean bags would make this bag better, but it is a good enough bag for the job.

text_fidelity_a: 13 Fishing - Kalon A - Spinning Reels We have been waiting for the chance to review these 13 Fishing Kalon reels.  We finally got the chance this past weekend to get out and test the 4.0, the 2.0 and then this 0.5 right here.  Of the three, this one is about as standard as they come.  Nothing fancy about this one, and there were several things that made me feel like this reel would actually be the most effective starter reel for kids.  By saying that, I don't mean to imply that it looks like a kids toy reel, I just mean in the way that the construction is done to where you don't have anything to really worry about getting all scratched up, plus the plastic handle has more of a rubber grip for non-slip, little wet hands.  I found that quite nice so that was one of my first thoughts.  We had our 11 year old start out with this reel, and he has had his fair share of fishing excursions so he is not entirely a new angler, and he immediately reported that he love how light the feel was, the crank was smooth, that the retrieve was smooth, and that he didn't have some of the reel tangle or hitching that he has with his other reel.  Not entirely sure how long this will hold up only time will tell of course as with any other reel.  For a more affordable reel, this seems like it is going to do well for him.  Fishing gear has become quite costly, as with everything else these days, and I feel like this reel for our purpose, still falls in line with the other 2 Kalon reels we have tested out this weekend, just as budget friendly and would also make a nice gift.  Your more professional anglers probably would pass on this reel, and that's perfectly okay.  Construction of a reel is pretty important, but also, aesthetics tend to play a part even if they try to tell you it doesn't.  So if I were to have anything objective to add to this review, it would only be that it looks a little on the cheap side, but I can say, I tried it out too and it does not perform cheaply.  I do recommend this reel especially for beginners and I hope you find this review helpful.

text_fidelity_a:
Energizer TAC-R 700 LED Tactical Flashlight, Bright Rechargeable Flashlight for Emergencies and Camping Gear, Water Resistant EDC Flashlight, USB Cable Included, Pack of 1 I like this flashlight. It is made in China, but feels sturdier than the $10 generic non-rechargeable flashlights that I also see on Amazon. I trust the charging circuitry on an Energizer-branded flashlight more than on a generic flashlight (and the batteries in these flashlights are powerful enough that safe recharging is important). The flashlight has 3 brightness modes plus one flashing mode. I like that the strobe mode needs to be activated by a double-tap on the power button, so I am very unlikely to get that mode accidentally (and I hate flashlights that start strobing when I don't want them to). The steady mode has a nice wide uniform beam despite the flashlight having a compact size (1.2 inches at the widest). A lot of cheaper flashlights are bright only in the center, then fade rapidly towards the sides. I find the uniform beam to be much more useful.

Yes, the battery is not replaceable and the whole unit will have to be discarded when the battery no longer holds it charge. Hopefully that will be after hundreds of charges, which is many years for me and I'll probably lose the flashlight before that happens. If you use your flashlight for hours every day, then this may be a bigger concern to you.
text_fidelity_b: Energizer TAC-R 700 LED Tactical Flashlight, Bright Rechargeable Flashlight for Emergencies and Camping Gear, Water Resistant EDC Flashlight, USB Cable Included, Pack of 1

Sanlan Resistance Bands Set with Workout Bar, Pilates Bar Kit Exercise Elastic Bands with Handles & Door Anchor for Full Body Strength Training, Home Gym Equipment If you’re someone who wants a strength- based workout, you know that using weights is the normal and common way to go. If you don’t have weights, there is an alternative that some say is just as good, and that is using resistance bands like this set, sold by the Sanlan Store.

With this set, you get multiple bands, a bar to hook them on, and a few accessories like ankle straps, handles, and a door anchor. The bands, colored yellow, green, red, blue, and black, offer different levels of resistance. You can start out low, with just a band or two, then gradually combine more bands for a more strenuous workout.

Using resistance bands is something completely new to me and there are many good reasons to like this or even prefer this to using actual weights. The top reason is the ease of working out anytime, anyplace. Because there is no actual weight, you can take your carrying bag and bands most anywhere. They are lightweight and take up little space. You can then remove them from the bag, hook the bands to the bar, and begin your workout. I don’t really have any basis for comparison, since this is something new to me, but the bands are durable and made to last. I don’t have any worries that they will break, so I can workout with peace of mind.

Some exercise bands are nothing more than bands, but this set comes complete with a bar, so it’s all set for you to use. Of course, you don’t have to use the bar- there are other exercises you can do that do not require the bar. But I like that the set has everything you need for a varied workout.

Free weights, barbells, and dumbbells are still the most common way to weight train, but there is something to be said for using resistance bands instead. I feel safer using these bands than I do using free weights and I like that I can easily take them most anyplace. It’s a quality set and a good one for those who want to improve their physical fitness.
text_fidelity_b: Sanlan Resistance Bands Set with Workout Bar, Pilates Bar Kit Exercise Elastic Bands with Handles & Door Anchor for Full Body Strength Training, Home Gym Equipment

Bowflex Treadmill Series I am a middle aged marathon runner. I have been having some issues with my heel so I got this treadmill with the hope that it will be less impact than running outside. I've found it to be a good machine with a nice running surface and an intuitive interface.

The running surface is 20 inches by 60 inches. It's a very large and comfortable surface. The surface absorbs your foot strikes very well, but it is not bouncy. There is also good traction on the running surface so there's no danger of slipping even when you start to sweat.

The assembled weight is 280 pounds, so this is a very sturdy and stable unit. I was able to assemble it with the help of my wife. I'd recommend that you have a space cleared out for it when the delivery people arrive. The closer they can put the treadmill to where you want it, the better. Overall assembly was easy, but it took a couple of hours. The treadmill comes with all the tools you need to put it together. The manual is easy to follow.

Once the treadmill has been put together, you can separate it into two components with relative ease. You just have to detach the console cable and remove the console structure with a few screws. This will allow you to move it without completely disassembling the whole unit.

There are buttons on either side of the touch screen. On the right are the buttons for treadmill speed, and on the left are the buttons for incline. There are also thumb buttons on the console so you can increase and decrease your speed at smaller increments. The unit also includes an emergency shut off that connects to your shirt with a clip.

When you select a speed, the treadmill accelerates to that speed relatively fast. I actually like this feature because it helps you get up to pace quickly if you're trying to run an interval.

The console is basically a computer, so it will likely have to download some updates the first time you turn it on. You'll also have to connect it to your Wi-Fi. There are a wide variety of workouts available on the console. I like the feature that allows you to watch videos of exotic settings as you run.

When I first tried to make a profile, the unit failed to send me a confirmation email. I believe the reason was that my password was only 6 characters instead of the required 8. I tried again after troubleshooting on the web page and didn’t have further issues. Once you create a profile, you have to do a 15 minute test workout so the console can start creating individualized workouts.

I was a little disappointed that you're unable to watch Netflix or Amazon prime unless you have a premium membership to the app. However, this unit has plenty of very nice features.

Overall, this is a high quality treadmill. It's comfortable to run on and the speed is consistent. I haven’t experienced any unexpected accelerations or decelerations. The incline feature allows you to challenge yourself, and the workouts are fun. This is a good product for getting into shape.
text_fidelity_b: Bowflex Treadmill Series

KastKing Sharky Spinning Fishing Reel Ultra Light Weight Freshwater Professional Open Face Reel With Features Found Only On Top Quality Penn Shimano Daiwa and Okuma Spinning Fishing Reels I love to go freshwater fishing and this weekend I approached the lake with a brand new weapon - a KastKing Sharky 6000 spinning reel. This is a serious reel that made a good day of fishing even better.

I will start by saying that even though it is approximately the same weight as my primary reel - a KastKing Orcas 4000 - it is significantly larger. I spooled on over 200 yards of 10-lb. test fluorocarbon line and it still had room for more line on it. I put it on an 8' limber rod and headed out to a productive spot.

I am very fussy about my reels and I expect them to meet several criteria. I want a good cast range, a smooth cast, smooth retrieve, quiet operation and a zero-reverse clutch. There has to be enough clearance between my knuckles and the bail to keep it from rapping me on the knuckles when I retrieve. And finally, the drag has to work and be easy to set. The Sharky met every one of these requirements.

I learned fast (and the hard way) that the reel is more than accommodating when it comes to casting and more than once I sent my lures into the trees instead of to the edge of the bank when I was unable to hit the bank with other reels on identical rods. This required a little adjustment on my part but it meant I did not have to work as hard and it also meant I could hit farther targets when I wanted to. So, when I fish from the bank I have a better range into whatever water I am fishing.

The retrieve is glassy smooth and very fast too. Not once did I have a problem with snarled line on the retrieve when I had near-zero load which is a problem on some reels. I like that I could bring in the line very quickly when needed (like for grabbing the net to assist another fisherman). The reel is quiet when spinning - not silent, but quiet.

When the ant-reverse clutch is engaged there is no reverse at all. To me this is a sign that the reel is quality made and is assembled well. I really, really dislike reels that do not have a zero-reverse clutch, and even worse is a reel that has one but it still has just a little play in it. The Sharky’s zero-reverse is solid and works exactly like it’s supposed to work - absolutely zero reverse.

The bail spins an inch or so away from my knuckles but never once has it hit my hand when spinning.

The drag set is uniform and smooth and does not really get harder to turn until close to the end of the tightening range.

In appearance this is a very attractive reel, black and red with a little bit of chrome. It is surprisingly lightweight for the size. I have bigger hands than average so a reel this size that doesn’t add much more weight is very welcome.

The reel helped me land a good variety of fish including largemouth bass, crappie and a near-citation yellow perch. The most exciting catch was a largemouth bass which was not huge but not small either and provided the best test of the reel under stress, and the reel brought this fish to the boat easily without incident. Even under the load of a fighting bass the reel was just as smooth in operation as when retrieving a test plug.

I am very, very pleased with the Sharky 6000 and will be using it again in the same lake in a few weeks. It has not let me down even once and it works very well. If you want a larger reel that works great and does not add a lot of weight to your gear, take a very close look at this reel.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: KastKing Sharky Spinning Fishing Reel Ultra Light Weight Freshwater Professional Open Face Reel With Features Found Only On Top Quality Penn Shimano Daiwa and Okuma Spinning Fishing Reels

Aerobie Superdisc Ultra, Colors May Vary I thought the Aerobie couldn't be beat. I mean, it's soft, flexible, fun, soars for ages but is easily controlled in smaller spaces too.

But this Superdisc might just improve on the original. There's something very satisfying about the traditional frisbee shape that the Aerobie original never captured. Yet the traditional frisbee hurts my hands when I catch it. I have very little fat or muscle on my fingers, and so when a frisbee knocks my hand the wrong way, I get huge purple bruises and welts on my hands and wrists which make playing frisbee with a traditional frisbee not very fun.

The Superdisc, by contract, has a soft rim of that Aerobie rubberized plastic which makes it easier to catch without hurting delicate hands. It flies forever, and the weight balance feels perfect. I played this indoors, in a tiny park, and at the beach over distances so large that we couldn't even shout at one another. It worked great and was a blast in every setting.

Only thing I wish is that we could choose our colors. I'd like the girly hot pink, while my partner hoped for a blue. We got a yellow one. You get what you get, apparently.

Overall this is well worth the price, and even if you throw it in the ocean as we did with our last Aerobie, it's still well worth it if you get at least a few games with it. We won't be without one now.
text_fidelity_b: Aerobie Superdisc Ultra, Colors May Vary
